hero.title: Playtribe
hero.description: Playtribe started from a simple observation: finding people to play with is still surprisingly difficult when you move to a new city, have an irregular schedule, or do not already belong to a sports group. I designed and developed the app as a social layer for local sport, exploring how a digital product could make the first step feel less awkward and a new connection feel more natural.
benefits: A trust layer for new connections

story.title: Designing a lower-friction way to meet
story.intro: The project began with a tension: people want to be more active and social, but the first step is often the hardest one.
paragraphs: I wanted to explore what a sports product could feel like if it started from social confidence rather than performance. The design needed to make a new activity feel approachable, while still giving people enough context to decide if a plan was right for them.

That led to a visual language built around warm surfaces, editorial typography and clear moments of action. The product combines discovery, event creation and community trust into one coherent experience, with the interface doing the work of reducing uncertainty.

tech_stack.title: How it was built
tech_stack.intro: The project combined product thinking, interface design and cross-platform development. I worked across the experience from the first product idea to the interaction model and technical implementation.

cards.title: Frontend
cards.text: A cross-platform Flutter application with reusable widgets, responsive mobile screens, stateful navigation and interaction patterns shaped around the product flow.

cards.title: Backend
cards.text: A Supabase-backed architecture for authentication, profiles, events, chat, realtime updates and secure access to product data.

cards.title: Tools & process
cards.text: The work moved between product definition, UI systems, prototyping, visual assets and release preparation, keeping the design and implementation in conversation.
